narrative: The macro decodes the dropped files using Windows certutil.exe with the following commands (certutil.exe is a legitimate built-in command-line program to manage certificates in Windows): C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe" /c certutil -decode C:\ProgramData\padre1.txt C:\ProgramData\\GUP.txt C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe" /c. Figure 9: Example of callback Earlier versions of [REDACTED_MALWARE] used the hard-coded string “this is the encrypt key” for Blowfish encryption when communicating with a C2. The macro drops three PEM files, padre1.txt, padre2.txt, and padre3.txt, to the victim’s %TEMP% folder and then copies them from %TEMP% to the %AllUserProfile% folder.
